display.title: Episode 222: The Secret of the Empty Fireplace (Yud-Gimmel Nissan)
display.summary_short: On the Tzemach Tzedek's yahrzeit, the night of bedikas chametz: how young Menachem Mendel hid in a fireplace to hear his grandfather teach Torah, plus a checklist for getting ready for Pesach.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Yud-Gimmel Nissan, the yahrzeit of the Tzemach Tzedek, the night before Erev Pesach. After a final reminder of the Tzivos Hashem 'Pesach Experience' and the Hakochainik march, Uncle Yossi asks children to say, 'When will my deeds reach the deeds of my fathers?' A visiting father and his children join the program, and his daughter leads the Shema. The story: nine-year-old Menachem Mendel, too young to join the Torah lessons the Alter Rebbe gave his children, secretly crawls into the empty fireplace between the rooms to listen. One cold evening the butler lights the fire without seeing him; burning logs fly out, and the boy is found motionless until the Alter Rebbe lays his hand on his head and he wakes. His love of Torah reached mesiras nefesh, like Avraham Avinu in the fiery furnace. Uncle Yossi reflects that every child's hidden love for Hashem can be lit like a candle, closes the 'My Sefer Torah' contest, and goes through the Pesach checklist: cleaning, selling and searching for and burning chametz, Yom Tov candles, eruv tavshilin, and eating matzah at both Sedarim.
display.lesson: Love Torah so much that you will do anything to learn more; every Jewish child's love for Hashem can be lit like a candle.

advisories.note: A boy hiding in a fireplace is caught when the fire is lit and is found unconscious; he is revived.
